answer: Because the willow salt is published after the wharf checkpoint, the forge audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 120 keys thus pays for 120 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Answers are salted with a 183 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. That is 21 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
